question_groups.title: EMC assessment and technical documentation (Annex I, Annex II)

questions.label: What kind of equipment is the product under the EMC Directive?
questions.guidance: Apparatus is a finished appliance, or a combination of them, made available as a single functional unit to end users, that can generate electromagnetic disturbance or whose operation can be affected by it. A fixed installation is a particular combination of apparatus and other devices assembled and intended to be used permanently at a predefined location. A component or sub-assembly that is only built into other equipment by its maker, and has no direct function for an end user, is not apparatus. Equipment that by its nature cannot cause disturbance and is not affected by it (for example passive items such as simple cables or resistive heaters) is outside the directive. Kits for radio amateurs that are not sold commercially are also outside it.

questions.label: How do you show that the apparatus meets the EMC protection requirements?
questions.guidance: Harmonised standards cited in the Official Journal give a presumption of conformity for the phenomena they cover. Where none is applied, or only part of it, your EMC assessment and technical documentation must show how the protection requirements are met.

questions.label: Do the instructions give the information needed to use the apparatus as intended, including any precautions when assembling, installing, maintaining or using it and any restriction on use in residential environments?
questions.guidance: Answer no if the instructions are silent on EMC-related precautions or on restrictions such as use only in industrial environments.

questions.label: Is the fixed installation's compliance with the protection requirements documented, with a responsible person identified?
questions.guidance: A fixed installation is not CE marked and has no declaration of conformity. It must be installed to good engineering practice, respecting the information on the intended use of its components, and the documentation must be kept available to the authorities for as long as it operates.

finding_rules.message: Radio equipment: electromagnetic compatibility is assessed under RED Art. 3(1)(b), not the EMC Directive. Use the RED package.

Radio hardware present but disabled (physically, or until a manufacturer update): the product is under the EMC Directive, not RED, while the radio stays disabled. Enabling it makes the product radio equipment and requires re-assessment under RED.
Excluded on the strength of the Commission's EMC Guide. Keep the reasoning (for example why the equipment cannot cause or suffer disturbance) on record, because the authorities can ask for it.
Fixed installation: no CE marking or EU declaration of conformity. The apparatus built into it must meet the directive on its own, and the installation must follow good engineering practice.
Document how the fixed installation meets the protection requirements and identify a responsible person; keep the documentation available to the authorities.
No presumption of conformity for the phenomena not covered by harmonised standards: the EMC assessment and technical documentation must show how the protection requirements are met for them.
Complete the technical documentation, including the EMC assessment, before placing the apparatus on the market.
Draw up the EU declaration of conformity before placing the apparatus on the market.
Affix the CE marking before placing the apparatus on the market.
Mark a type, batch or serial number and the manufacturer's name and postal address on the units, or on the packaging or documents where that is not possible.
Supply the information needed to use the apparatus as intended, including EMC precautions and any restriction on use in residential environments.
Check the CE marking, the documents and instructions and the identification of the manufacturer and importer before supplying the apparatus.
Placing the apparatus under your own name or modifying it makes you the manufacturer: the manufacturer's obligations apply to you.
Open-source steward is not a role under the EMC Directive. Answer as manufacturer, importer, distributor or authorised representative for this product.
All units were placed on the market before 20 April 2016: they may still be made available if they conform to the previous directive, 2004/108/EC.
